pencereler.0-5: A fatigue crack grew until the tyre broke free. A German high-speed train derailed
pencereler.5-12: and slammed into a road bridge. The bridge collapsed onto the carriages, and one hundred one people were killed.
pencereler.12-20: It began with a single wheel. The wheels had a steel tyre cushioned by rubber. That design came from trams, not high-speed
pencereler.20-30: trains. It jammed into the points and derailed the train. German high-speed trains switched to solid steel wheels.

segmentler.metin: The ICE at Eschede derailed and crashed into a bridge.
It took only a fatigue crack in a steel wheel tyre.
So how could a fatigue crack in a steel wheel tyre do this?

The answer is fatigue fracture of a rubber-cushioned wheel's outer tyre, which then struck the points — and it is why resilient wheels were replaced with solid monobloc wheels on German high-speed trains.
